body.statement:
There are universal finite constants \(M>0\) and \(\rho_0\in(0,1/16]\) such that, simultaneously for every \(1\le\ell\le L\), every \(0<\rho\le\rho_0\), and every \((c_{\ell1},c_{\ell2},c_{\ell3})\in[1/2,4]^3\),
\[
\left|u^2 C_{\rho,\ell}+1\right|\le \frac{M}{u^2}.
\]
The same bound holds on both exact cancellation planes \(x_\ell=0\) and \(z_\ell=0\).  Equivalently, uniformly on the complete coefficient box, \(C_{\rho,\ell}=-u^{-2}+O(u^{-4})\) as \(\rho\downarrow0\), without any division by \(A_\ell\).
body.proof_tex:
We give a common-cutoff proof and keep all estimates uniform in the coefficient box.  For \(v>0\), the substitution \(w=v+s/v\) gives the exact identity
\[
\frac{\Phi(-v)}{\phi(v)}
=\frac1v\int_0^\infty e^{-s}e^{-s^2/(2v^2)}\,ds.
\]
Taylor's theorem at a nonnegative argument gives
\[
e^{-a}=1-a+\frac{a^2}{2}+r(a),\qquad |r(a)|\le\frac{a^3}{6}.
\]
Since \(\int_0^\infty e^{-s}s^k\,ds=k!\), integration produces
\[
\frac{\Phi(-v)}{\phi(v)}
=\frac1v\left(1-v^{-2}+3v^{-4}+\varepsilon_v\right),
\qquad |\varepsilon_v|\le15v^{-6}.
\tag{1}
\]
For \(v\ge2\), the bracket in (1) is bounded away from zero.  Multiplication of finite polynomials, followed by the identity
\[
\frac1{1+h}=1-h+h^2-\frac{h^3}{1+h},
\]
applied to \(h=-v^{-2}+3v^{-4}+\varepsilon_v\), shows that there is an absolute \(K_0<\infty\) such that
\[
\left|m(-v)-\left(v+v^{-1}-2v^{-3}\right)\right|\le K_0v^{-5}.
\tag{2}
\]
The exact identity \(m'(-v)=-m(-v)\{m(-v)-v\}\), rather than differentiation of a remainder, then implies for another absolute \(K_1\)
\[
\left|m'(-v)-\left(-1+v^{-2}\right)\right|\le K_1v^{-4}.
\tag{3}
\]

It remains to put every quantile in (2)--(3) under one cutoff.  Let \(u=-q(\rho)\), and for \(|a|\le\log4\) put \(v_a=-q(\rho e^a)\).  Choose \(u_0\) so large that
\[
e^{3u_0^2/8}>4,
\qquad u_0\ge4.
\]
Because \(m(-w)>w\),
\[
\log\frac{\Phi(-u/2)}{\Phi(-u)}
=\int_{u/2}^{u}m(-w)\,dw
>\frac{3u^2}{8}.
\]
Thus, whenever \(u\ge u_0\), all probabilities between \(\rho/2\) and \(4\rho\) have inverse-tail magnitudes at least \(u/2\).  Also
\[
\frac{d}{da}v_a=-\frac1{m(-v_a)},
\]
and integration along the interval joining \(0\) and \(a\) yields
\[
|v_a-u|\le\frac{2\log4}{u}.
\tag{4}
\]
Every geometric interpolation \(c_3^{1-s}c_1^s\) and \(c_3^{1-t}c_2^t\) remains in \([1/2,4]\).  Hence (4) applies to the two denominator quantiles in the definition of \(B_{\rho,\ell}\).  It also shows that the negative of the combined numerator argument
\[
q(\rho c_3^{1-s}c_1^s)+q(\rho c_3^{1-t}c_2^t)-q(\rho c_3)
\]
equals \(u+O(u^{-1})\), uniformly in \(s,t\in[0,1]\), the pair index, and all three coefficients.  Increasing \(u_0\), if necessary, makes all these magnitudes at least \(2\).

Substitution into (2)--(3) now gives constants \(K_2,K_3<\infty\), independent of all indices and coefficients, for which
\[
m\{q(\rho c_3^{1-s}c_1^s)\}=u+O(u^{-1}),\qquad
m\{q(\rho c_3^{1-t}c_2^t)\}=u+O(u^{-1}),
\]
and
\[
\frac{m'\{q(\rho c_3^{1-s}c_1^s)+q(\rho c_3^{1-t}c_2^t)-q(\rho c_3)\}}
{m\{q(\rho c_3^{1-s}c_1^s)\}m\{q(\rho c_3^{1-t}c_2^t)\}}
=-u^{-2}+E_{s,t},\qquad |E_{s,t}|\le K_3u^{-4}.
\tag{5}
\]
Integrating (5) over the unit square proves
\[
B_{\rho,\ell}=-u^{-2}+O(u^{-4})
\tag{6}
\]
uniformly on the entire coefficient box.  In particular, this step did not divide by \(x_\ell z_\ell\).

Finally, \(|A_\ell|\le(\log8)^2\), so (6) gives \(|A_\ell B_{\rho,\ell}|=O(u^{-2})\).  From the integral representation of \(\psi\),
\[
|\psi(w)-1|
\le \int_0^1 t|w|e^{|w|}\,dt
\le\tfrac12|w|e^{|w|}.
\]
Consequently \(\psi(A_\ell B_{\rho,\ell})=1+O(u^{-2})\), and
\[
C_{\rho,\ell}=B_{\rho,\ell}\psi(A_\ell B_{\rho,\ell})
=-u^{-2}+O(u^{-4})
\]
with one common constant.  Choose \(\rho_0=\min\{1/16,\Phi(-u_0)\}\) and enlarge the finite constant to \(M\).  When \(x_\ell=0\) or \(z_\ell=0\), the definition gives \(A_\ell=0\) and \(\psi(A_\ell B_{\rho,\ell})=1\), while (5)--(6) are unchanged.  This proves the claimed certificate on both planes.
